page.layout: One page of running text in a single column; running head at top with the page number at top right; margin notes in the right margin (three side notes); catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: ritoneo nata, stomachi quasi commune inuolucrum.
Orificia ventriculi sunt, Ventriculi orificia. quæ cibo coquendo aditum, costoue exitum præbent.
Hæc orificia sunt rugosa & crafsiora, fibrisq; orbicularibus prædita, quæ natura iubente dilatari arctariuè possunt, adeoque permittunt cibos ingredi & egredi.
Superius continuum est Oesophago amplius, quo cibus ore masticatus & ventriculo concoquendus recipitur.
Inferius, nempe Pyloros, arctius est angusto collo obductum, & leviter quasi sursum reflexum, per quod chylus concoctus ad intestina delabitur.
Figura ventriculi oblonga est, instar lyripipii, cum ratione capacitatis, tum ratione orificiorum. Ventriculi figura.
Locum in ventre medium occupat, fere inter Lienem & Epar, sub diaphragmate.
main_text.head: CAPUT XLI. DE OESOPHAGO, ET INTESTINIS GRACILIORIBUS.

page.notes: The word "Admi-" at the foot is the start of a catchword ("Admiranda"), printed as a hyphenated break; it is recorded here and in the catchword area, not repeated. The margin notes "Ventriculi orificia." and "Ventriculi figura." are the two clear side notes; a faint third note at mid-right is too blurred to read and is omitted. Show-through from the reverse page appears throughout and is excluded. The heading "CAPUT XLI. DE OESOPHAGO, ET INTESTINIS GRACILIORIBUS." is set in small capitals with the final line in italic; the italic continuation reads "stinis gracilioribus." and has been joined to the heading. The word "stinis" is partly cut by the page edge and is uncertain: [?]
